By creating an account, creating a course, or otherwise using Pockit, you agree to these Terms. If you don't agree, please don't use Pockit.

1. Eligibility

You must be at least 16 years old to create a Pockit account or course. If you're using Pockit on behalf of a school, employer, or other organisation, you confirm you have the authority to agree to these Terms on their behalf.

2. Your Account

You're responsible for keeping your account credentials secure and for all activity that happens under your account. Let us know promptly if you think your account has been compromised.

3. Your Content

You keep ownership of the courses, lesson cards, text, images, and other material you create or upload ("Your Content"). By creating or uploading Content, you grant Pockit a licence to store, display, and make it available as directed by you — including to anyone you choose to share a course with via Pockit's sharing features. This licence exists only so we can operate the service; it ends when you delete the relevant Content or your account, except where a copy reasonably persists in backups for a limited period, or where you've shared it and the recipient retains their own copy.

You're solely responsible for Your Content and for making sure you have the right to use anything you include in it.

4. Content Standards

When creating a course, you agree not to include:

5. No AI-Agent-Created Courses

Pockit is for people creating their own courses, using the Pockit editor themselves. You may not use an AI agent, bot, script, or other automated tool to generate, populate, or bulk-create course content, or to otherwise interact with Pockit's editing features programmatically in place of a human user. This doesn't stop you personally using an AI tool as a writing aid before typing or pasting your own material in — what's not allowed is an autonomous agent operating Pockit, or generating substantial course content, on your behalf without a person actually doing the creating.

6. Course Sharing

Pockit lets you share a course with other people you invite by email. If you invite someone, you're responsible for making sure you have a legitimate basis to share that content with them. Recipients get read-only access to the course you've shared, until you revoke it.
